causes: Battery health has degraded below 80% capacity
Background apps running continuously and consuming power
Screen brightness or always-on display settings too high
Faulty battery failing to hold charge across cycles
beginner_fixes: Go to Settings → Battery and check battery health percentage
Enable battery saver or low-power mode immediately
Reduce screen brightness to 40–50% and disable always-on display
Turn off Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and location services when not in use
intermediate_fixes: Review which apps consume the most battery in Settings → Battery → Usage
Disable background app refresh for all non-essential applications
Check for and install any pending operating system updates
Perform a full discharge-to-zero then full recharge cycle to recalibrate
advanced_fixes: Run a battery diagnostic using a third-party app (e.g. AccuBattery on Android)
If battery health is below 80%, replace the battery — phone/mail-in services cost $30–$60
Factory reset as a last resort if software corruption is suspected
doNot: Do not charge overnight repeatedly — it accelerates battery degradation
Do not use fast charging constantly; standard charging is gentler on the battery
Do not ignore battery health below 75% — it will worsen quickly
lifespanNotes: A replaced battery restores full-day performance. Original batteries typically last 2–3 years under normal use.

causes: Charging port clogged with lint, dust, or debris
Damaged or counterfeit charging cable not delivering adequate power
Faulty power adapter or USB port on the charger
Charging port physically damaged or with bent pins
Software glitch preventing the charge management system from activating
beginner_fixes: Try a different certified charging cable — this resolves the issue ~40% of the time
Try a different power adapter and a different wall outlet
Inspect the charging port with a torch for visible lint or debris
Gently clean the charging port with a dry toothpick or soft brush — do not use metal objects
intermediate_fixes: Force restart the device while plugged in (hold Power + Volume Down for 10 seconds)
Try charging from a computer USB port to isolate whether the adapter is faulty
Check if wireless charging works — if yes, the physical port is the issue
Update device software, as some OS bugs affect charge detection
advanced_fixes: Use compressed air to clear the port (brief bursts only, hold can upright)
If port is physically damaged or corroded, a port replacement costs $40–$80 at a repair shop
If water damage is suspected, do not attempt to charge — leave in dry rice or silica gel for 48 hours first
doNot: Do not insert metal objects into the charging port to clean it
Do not charge a device you suspect has water damage
Do not bend or force the cable into the port if resistance is felt
lifespanNotes: A charging port replacement is a cost-effective repair. A clean port and quality cable typically solve this without hardware work.

causes: Physical impact from dropping the device
Pressure applied to the screen while in a pocket or bag
Existing micro-crack that propagated under stress
Absence of a screen protector reducing impact resistance
beginner_fixes: Apply a clear adhesive screen protector immediately to prevent the crack spreading and protect fingers from glass
Check if the touch layer still functions — tap and swipe across all areas
Back up all data urgently in case the display fails completely
Check if your device warranty or phone insurance covers screen damage
intermediate_fixes: Get a repair quote from the manufacturer — official repairs often include a warranty
Compare with certified third-party repair shops, which are typically 30–40% cheaper
Check iFixit.com for your specific model to assess DIY replacement difficulty
advanced_fixes: Screen replacement is a hardware repair — order the correct OEM-spec display for your exact model
DIY replacement requires a heat gun, suction cup, spudger, and precision screwdrivers; cost is $40–$120 in parts
For flagship phones with Face ID or under-display fingerprint readers, always use a certified technician to avoid losing biometric functionality
doNot: Do not continue using a heavily cracked screen — glass shards can cause injury
Do not apply super glue or tape over the screen — it damages the digitizer
Do not attempt screen replacement without an anti-static mat if you have no experience
lifespanNotes: A professional screen replacement restores the device to near-new condition. The repair pays for itself if the device is under 2 years old.

causes: Loose or partially disconnected display ribbon cable
Software or graphics driver bug causing refresh rate instability
GPU or display controller hardware fault
Screen damaged internally from an impact without visible cracks
beginner_fixes: Force restart the device to rule out a temporary software glitch
Check if flickering occurs in Safe Mode — if not, a third-party app is the cause
Reduce screen brightness and disable adaptive brightness to test if it's display-load related
Check for operating system updates — graphics bugs are frequently patched
intermediate_fixes: Boot into Safe Mode and monitor for 30 minutes; if flickering stops, uninstall recently installed apps
Perform a display calibration if available in developer options
Back up data immediately — flickering often precedes full display failure
advanced_fixes: If flickering followed a drop, the ribbon cable connection may need reseating — this requires screen removal
A display replacement resolves hardware-based flickering; costs $80–$150 depending on model
If under warranty, submit for a manufacturer warranty claim before spending on repairs
doNot: Do not ignore persistent flickering — it often precedes complete display failure
Do not attempt to reseat the ribbon cable without proper ESD protection
Do not use the phone for extended periods if the flicker is worsening
lifespanNotes: Software-caused flickering is fully resolvable. Hardware-caused flickering requires screen replacement but is a well-understood repair.

causes: CPU-intensive apps running in the background (games, video encoding, mining apps)
Defective battery generating excess heat during charging
Blocked ventilation or use in a high-ambient-temperature environment
Malware or a runaway process consuming 100% CPU
beginner_fixes: Immediately remove any phone case and place the device on a cool, flat surface
Close all apps and stop any active downloads or streaming
Disconnect the charger and do not charge while the device is hot
Do not place in a fridge or freezer — rapid temperature change causes condensation damage
intermediate_fixes: Check CPU and battery temperature using a diagnostics app
Review battery usage for any app consuming abnormally high CPU in the background
Scan for malware — cryptocurrency mining malware is a common hidden cause
Check if the phone overheats only while charging — this points to a faulty charger or battery
advanced_fixes: If a specific app is consistently causing heat, uninstall it and report to the developer
A swollen battery (visible as a bulge on the back) requires immediate professional replacement — do not charge
Thermal paste replacement is not applicable to phones; if hardware is the root cause, a motherboard or battery replacement is required
doNot: Do not use the device while it is significantly overheating — it can damage the battery permanently
Do not place in a freezer or submerge in water to cool it
Do not ignore a swollen battery — it is a fire and explosion risk
lifespanNotes: Software-caused overheating is fully resolvable. If a battery is causing heat, replace it promptly to avoid further damage to internal components.

causes: Direct submersion or heavy water exposure exceeding the device's IP rating
Liquid ingress through charging port, speaker grille, or SIM slot
Corrosion developing on internal circuit boards after exposure
No IP rating on the device providing any water resistance
beginner_fixes: Power off the device immediately — do NOT press power if it is on; just hold to power off
Remove SIM card and SIM tray to allow drainage
Shake the device gently with the port facing down to expel visible water
Pat dry with a lint-free cloth — do not rub
intermediate_fixes: Place in a sealed bag of silica gel packets (not rice — rice is a myth and adds starch) for 48–72 hours
Place near (not on) a gentle heat source such as a warm lamp to aid evaporation
Do not attempt to power on for at least 48 hours after drying
advanced_fixes: Take to a professional repair shop that offers ultrasonic cleaning — this removes corrosion from the board
Professional board-level repair (cleaning + corrosion treatment) costs $50–$120
If the device was submerged in salt water or another liquid, DIY recovery is unlikely — go straight to a professional
doNot: Do not charge the device until you are certain it is completely dry — this causes short circuits
Do not put in rice — it provides minimal absorption and can introduce starch into ports
Do not use a hair dryer on hot setting — heat accelerates corrosion
lifespanNotes: Recovery success drops significantly after 24 hours. Act within the first hour for the best outcome. Devices with IP67 or IP68 ratings have a higher survival rate.

causes: Device stuck in headphone mode due to debris in the audio jack
Speaker grille blocked by lint or dirt reducing sound output
Volume accidentally muted via hardware switch or software setting
Speaker hardware failure from impact or water exposure
beginner_fixes: Check that the mute/silent switch is in the correct position (iPhones)
Verify volume is turned up and Do Not Disturb mode is off
Plug in headphones and remove them — this can reset a stuck headphone-mode state
Test sound in multiple apps (music, video, phone call) to isolate the issue
intermediate_fixes: Clean the speaker grille gently with a soft, dry brush
Restart the device and test again
Check audio output settings — it may be routed to Bluetooth or a connected device
Test with headphones — if audio works through headphones, the issue is the speaker hardware
advanced_fixes: A cotton swab very lightly dampened with isopropyl alcohol can clean a blocked headphone jack
Speaker replacement is a straightforward repair; costs $30–$80 at a shop or $15–$30 DIY
If audio works on calls but not media (or vice versa), the device has separate earpiece and loudspeaker — identify which one is faulty
doNot: Do not insert sharp objects into the speaker grille or headphone jack
Do not blow directly into the speaker grille — it can push debris further in
Do not attempt speaker replacement without following a model-specific guide
lifespanNotes: Cleaning resolves most audio issues. Hardware speaker replacement is a low-complexity repair with an excellent success rate.

causes: Software freeze or unresponsive process locking the UI thread
Screen protector interfering with capacitive touch sensitivity
Physical damage to the digitizer layer beneath the glass
Moisture or condensation on the screen disrupting touch detection
beginner_fixes: Force restart immediately: hold Power + Volume Down for 10–15 seconds
Remove any thick or cheap screen protector and test touch response
Dry the screen completely — moisture interferes with capacitive touch
Remove gloves or check you are using bare skin, not a stylus that isn't compatible
intermediate_fixes: Boot into Safe Mode to test if a third-party app is causing the freeze
Check for OS updates — touchscreen firmware bugs are patched regularly
If only part of the screen is unresponsive (dead zones), map the affected area — this is a digitizer hardware issue
advanced_fixes: A digitizer replacement is required for persistent dead zones — cost is $60–$150 combined with screen replacement
If the issue appeared after a drop, the ribbon cable connection may have come loose and requires professional reseating
Factory reset (after full backup) resolves software-caused unresponsiveness in most cases
doNot: Do not tap harder — extra force does not help capacitive screens and can damage the digitizer
Do not use the device for important tasks while the touchscreen is unreliable
Do not skip the backup before factory resetting
lifespanNotes: Software freezes are fully resolvable. Digitizer damage is a repairable hardware issue, though cost depends on whether the screen assembly must also be replaced.

causes: Camera app software crash or permissions issue
Dirty or smudged lens giving soft or blurry images
Hardware camera module damaged from a drop or impact
OIS (Optical Image Stabilisation) module failure causing blur on recent models
beginner_fixes: Force-close the camera app completely and reopen it
Clean the camera lens with a microfibre cloth — fingerprints are the most common cause of blurry photos
Restart the device and test the camera again
Check if the camera works in a third-party app (Snapchat, WhatsApp) to isolate whether it's the native app or hardware
intermediate_fixes: Go to Settings → Apps → Camera → Clear Cache, then relaunch
Check that the camera app has Camera permissions enabled in Settings → Privacy
Install pending software updates — camera processing bugs are frequently patched
Test front and rear cameras separately to identify which module is affected
advanced_fixes: If a black screen persists after all software steps, the camera module is likely physically damaged
Camera module replacement costs $50–$120 at a repair shop depending on the model
Water ingress into the camera module causes fogging on the inside — this requires module replacement, not cleaning
doNot: Do not attempt to clean inside the lens housing — the lens is sealed and internal cleaning requires full disassembly
Do not ignore fogging inside the lens — it indicates water ingress that will worsen
Do not use abrasive materials to clean the lens coating
lifespanNotes: Most camera issues are software-related and fully resolvable. Hardware module replacement is a standard repair offered by most phone repair shops.

causes: Completely discharged or failed battery
Faulty power adapter not delivering voltage to the laptop
RAM module seated incorrectly preventing POST completion
Corrupted bootloader or failed storage device
beginner_fixes: Plug into a known-working wall outlet using the original charger and leave for 30 minutes before trying again
While plugged in, hold the power button for 15 seconds to perform a hard reset
Remove the battery (if removable), hold power for 30 seconds, reconnect battery, then try to boot
Try a different power adapter — borrow one with the same voltage and connector if possible
intermediate_fixes: Connect to an external monitor — if the external display works, the laptop's internal display is the issue, not the board
Listen for POST beep codes on startup — beep patterns indicate specific hardware failures
If there are any lights or sounds on pressing power but no display, RAM may need reseating
Check the charging indicator LED — if it does not light when plugged in, the adapter or charging circuit is faulty
advanced_fixes: To reseat RAM: power off, remove battery, open bottom panel, press the RAM tabs outward, remove sticks, clean contacts with an eraser, reseat firmly
If the laptop reaches POST but fails to boot OS, boot from a USB recovery drive to diagnose the storage device
A faulty power jack (not adapter) requires soldering — seek a technician if the plug is loose inside the port
doNot: Do not attempt to short-circuit the battery terminals to force a start
Do not open the laptop near static-generating surfaces without an anti-static wrist strap
Do not assume the motherboard is dead before ruling out the power adapter, RAM, and storage
lifespanNotes: Most no-power issues are solved by adapter or RAM fixes. Motherboard-level failures are rare but possible on older devices — weigh repair cost against replacement value.

causes: Heatsink and fan clogged with dust blocking airflow
Thermal paste between CPU/GPU and heatsink dried out and no longer conducting heat
Laptop used on soft surfaces (bed, sofa) blocking the bottom intake vents
Background processes running the CPU at 100% continuously
beginner_fixes: Immediately place the laptop on a hard, flat surface — never use on a bed or pillow
Use compressed air to blow through all vents — you will see dust come out if this is the cause
Close unnecessary applications and check Task Manager (Windows) or Activity Monitor (Mac) for CPU hogs
Purchase a laptop cooling stand ($10–$25) — they reduce temperatures by 5–15°C
intermediate_fixes: Download HWMonitor (Windows) or iStatMenus (Mac) to read real CPU temperature readings
Set a power plan to 'Balanced' rather than 'High Performance' — reduces heat significantly
Schedule a full compressed air clean of all vents quarterly
Check for BIOS/firmware updates — many include improved fan curve profiles
advanced_fixes: Open the laptop bottom panel and manually clean the fan blades and heatsink with compressed air and a soft brush
If the laptop is 3+ years old, replace the thermal paste between the CPU/GPU and heatsink — this alone can drop temperatures 20–30°C
Thermal paste replacement requires: isopropyl alcohol (90%+), cotton swabs, thermal paste ($5–$15), and a screwdriver set
doNot: Do not block the vents with tape or stickers
Do not run the laptop at maximum load on a surface that blocks the bottom vents
Do not apply too much thermal paste — a pea-sized amount in the centre is correct
lifespanNotes: Thermal maintenance is the single highest-ROI repair on any laptop. Resolving overheating directly extends CPU and battery life by years.

diagnosis: Degraded performance — slow startup and application response
causes: Hard disk drive (HDD) instead of SSD causing slow read/write speeds
Insufficient RAM causing heavy disk paging under load
Startup programs overloading the system at boot
Malware or adware consuming CPU and memory resources
Storage near full — less than 10% free space severely impacts performance
beginner_fixes: Restart the laptop — many slowdowns are resolved by clearing RAM and restarting processes
Check disk space: if less than 10% is free, delete or move files immediately
Open Task Manager (Ctrl+Shift+Esc) and sort by CPU and Memory — kill any process using unusually high resources
Disable unnecessary startup programs: Task Manager → Startup tab → Disable all non-essential entries
intermediate_fixes: Run a full malware scan using Windows Defender or Malwarebytes Free
Clean up temporary files: Windows → Disk Cleanup → run on the C: drive
Check the storage drive health: run CrystalDiskInfo (Windows) or Disk Utility (Mac) — a failing drive causes severe slowdown
Increase virtual memory if RAM is consistently at 90%+ usage
advanced_fixes: Upgrading from an HDD to an SSD is the single most impactful upgrade — reduces boot time from 60+ seconds to under 10 seconds; cost $40–$100
Adding RAM (if slots available) from 4GB to 8GB or 8GB to 16GB resolves slowdown under multitasking; cost $20–$60
A clean OS reinstall removes all accumulated bloat — always back up first
doNot: Do not run 'registry cleaner' utilities — they rarely help and frequently cause new problems
Do not defragment an SSD — it shortens its lifespan; defragmentation is only for HDDs
Do not ignore a storage drive showing errors in disk health tools — data loss is imminent
lifespanNotes: An SSD upgrade transforms a slow 5-year-old laptop into a usable machine. It is almost always cheaper than buying a new laptop.

diagnosis: Laptop battery not charging when plugged in
causes: Power adapter damaged or not providing sufficient wattage for the laptop model
Battery driver or firmware issue preventing charge detection (common on Windows)
Battery has reached end of life and no longer accepts a charge
Charging circuit on the motherboard faulty
beginner_fixes: Inspect the power adapter and cable carefully for cuts, kinks, or fraying near the connectors
Try a different wall outlet and confirm the outlet works with another device
Check the charger wattage matches or exceeds your laptop's requirement (check the sticker on the bottom of the laptop)
Remove the battery (if removable), run on AC power only — if it works, the battery needs replacing
intermediate_fixes: On Windows: open Device Manager → Batteries → right-click 'Microsoft ACPI-Compliant Control Method Battery' → Uninstall → restart to reinstall the battery driver
Run the Windows power troubleshooter: Settings → System → Troubleshoot
Check the charge port on the laptop for bent pins or debris
Monitor charging behaviour: if it charges to 60% and stops, a charge limit may be enabled in manufacturer software
advanced_fixes: Battery replacement: most laptop batteries cost $30–$80 and are a common DIY repair with iFixit guides available for most models
If the AC adapter connector is loose inside the port, the DC jack needs soldering — take to a technician
Third-party chargers can damage the charging circuit — always use the manufacturer's rated wattage
doNot: Do not use a charger with a lower wattage than specified — it will charge very slowly or not at all and may overheat
Do not ignore a battery stuck at 0% — continued use risks deep discharge damage
Do not continue using a visibly damaged charging cable
lifespanNotes: Laptop batteries typically last 3–5 years. Replacement is straightforward and returns the laptop to full portability.

causes: Backlight inverter or LED backlight strip failure
Loose or damaged display cable (LVDS or eDP) running through the hinge
GPU failure preventing any video output
Display driver crash causing a black screen with the system still running
beginner_fixes: Connect an external monitor using HDMI or DisplayPort — if the external screen works, the issue is the internal display, not the GPU or OS
Ensure the laptop is powered on: listen for fan spin and drive activity sounds
Shine a torch at an angle against the screen in a dark room — very faint images indicate backlight failure, not display failure
Press Fn + the display toggle key (often F4 or F5) to cycle display modes
intermediate_fixes: If external monitor works: update or reinstall display drivers, then reboot
Check the hinge area — hinges that have been forced open too wide often damage the display cable
Hold the lid at different angles — if the image appears at some angles but not others, the cable is failing
advanced_fixes: Display cable replacement: run along the hinge, accessible by removing the screen bezel — cost $15–$30 in parts
Backlight replacement: if you see a very dim image, the backlight strip is failing — cost $20–$50 plus labour
Full screen panel replacement: $80–$300 depending on resolution and size; use the exact part number printed on the back of the current panel
doNot: Do not force the hinge open past 180 degrees — it stretches and damages the display cable
Do not conclude the motherboard is dead before testing with an external monitor
Do not peel the bezel off forcefully — use a plastic pry tool to avoid cracking it
lifespanNotes: Display cable and backlight replacements are cost-effective. A full panel replacement is worthwhile if the laptop is otherwise functional.

causes: Wi-Fi adapter driver corrupted or outdated
Physical Wi-Fi toggle switch accidentally disabled (present on some laptops)
Router or ISP outage rather than a laptop hardware issue
Wi-Fi card hardware failure
beginner_fixes: Check whether other devices connect to the same Wi-Fi — if not, the router is the issue
Toggle Airplane Mode on, wait 10 seconds, toggle off — this resets the wireless adapter
Check for a physical Wi-Fi switch on the side or front of the laptop
Restart both the router and the laptop
intermediate_fixes: Open Device Manager → Network Adapters → right-click Wi-Fi adapter → Update Driver
Run Windows Network Troubleshooter: Settings → System → Network → Troubleshoot
On Windows: open Command Prompt as administrator and run: netsh winsock reset then restart
Forget the network in Wi-Fi settings and reconnect fresh
advanced_fixes: Uninstall the Wi-Fi adapter from Device Manager then restart to force a clean driver reinstall
If the adapter does not appear in Device Manager at all, the Wi-Fi card may have failed — replacements cost $15–$40 and are user-installable on most laptops
An external USB Wi-Fi dongle ($10–$20) is an instant fix while you source a replacement card
doNot: Do not edit the registry to fix Wi-Fi unless following a verified guide — incorrect edits cause further issues
Do not assume the Wi-Fi card is dead before exhausting all driver and software fixes
Do not disable the network adapter in Device Manager thinking it will reset it — use Uninstall, not Disable
lifespanNotes: Wi-Fi issues are almost always software or driver related and fully resolvable. Hardware card failures are uncommon but cheap to fix.

causes: Liquid spilled on the keyboard shorting key circuits
Keyboard connector ribbon cable come loose from the motherboard
Filter Keys or Sticky Keys accessibility setting enabled causing delayed input
Individual key switches failing on older keyboards
beginner_fixes: Restart the laptop — driver crashes can disable the keyboard
Check Settings → Accessibility → Keyboard and disable Filter Keys and Sticky Keys
Plug in a USB keyboard — if it works, the internal keyboard is the hardware issue
Press and hold the affected key — sometimes debris beneath a key causes it to register as held
intermediate_fixes: Check Device Manager → Keyboards — if the keyboard shows a warning, uninstall and reinstall the driver
If keys are sticky or certain characters type randomly, liquid damage is likely — disconnect power and allow to dry for 48 hours
Check BIOS: if keyboard works during boot (BIOS screen) but not in Windows, it's a driver issue
advanced_fixes: Keyboard replacement is one of the most common laptop repairs — most models have keyboard assemblies available for $20–$60
On many models, the keyboard is attached to the top case and may need to be ordered as an assembly
Cleaning under keycaps with compressed air and isopropyl alcohol resolves sticky keys from minor spills
doNot: Do not pry keycaps off unless you have confirmed the replacement clips are available — they break easily
Do not continue using a keyboard if liquid was spilled — power off immediately to prevent board damage
Do not overlook the Filter Keys setting — it is a surprisingly common cause of keyboard issues
lifespanNotes: Keyboard replacement is affordable and straightforward. Most laptop keyboards are designed to be user-replaceable.

diagnosis: System crash — blue screen or kernel panic
causes: Faulty or failing RAM module causing memory errors
Storage drive failure or file system corruption
Outdated, incompatible, or corrupted device drivers
Overheating causing the CPU to reach thermal shutdown threshold
beginner_fixes: Photograph or write down the STOP code displayed on the blue screen — it identifies the specific cause
Check if the crash occurs after a specific action (plugging in a device, running an app) — this narrows the driver
Run Windows Update — many BSODs are caused by bugs fixed in recent patches
Check internal temperatures at the time of crash using HWMonitor
intermediate_fixes: Run Windows Memory Diagnostic: Start → search 'mdsched' → restart and run — this tests all RAM
Run CHKDSK on the system drive: open Command Prompt as admin → chkdsk C: /f /r → schedule on restart
Boot into Safe Mode — if crashes stop in Safe Mode, a third-party driver is the cause
Roll back any recently installed drivers in Device Manager
advanced_fixes: Download and run the WinDbg tool against the minidump files in C:\Windows\Minidump to identify the exact failing driver or module
If RAM is faulty, reseat both sticks. Test with one stick at a time to identify the bad module. Replacement DDR4/DDR5 RAM is $20–$60
If CHKDSK finds drive errors, back up all data immediately and clone the drive to a new SSD
doNot: Do not ignore recurring BSODs — they indicate a hardware failure that will worsen
Do not reinstall Windows as a first step — diagnose the root cause first or the issue will recur
Do not attempt to open minidump files in Notepad — use WinDbg or an online BSOD analyser
lifespanNotes: BSODs caused by drivers are fully resolvable. RAM or storage failures require hardware replacement but are straightforward to diagnose and fix.

causes: Condenser coils heavily coated with dust, blocking heat dissipation
Door seals worn or damaged, allowing warm air to enter continuously
Evaporator fan motor failed, preventing cold air circulation
Refrigerant leak causing gradual loss of cooling capacity
beginner_fixes: Check the temperature settings — the fridge compartment should be set to 2–4°C (37–40°F)
Ensure the fridge is not overpacked — air must circulate freely around food items
Check the door seals by closing the door on a piece of paper: if the paper slides out easily, the seal needs replacing
Verify the appliance is not positioned directly against a wall — leave at least 5cm clearance at the back and sides
intermediate_fixes: Unplug the fridge and vacuum or brush the condenser coils at the back or beneath the unit — dust buildup is the most common cause
Listen for the evaporator fan running inside the freezer compartment — if silent when the compressor is running, the fan motor has failed
Check if ice is building up excessively on the back wall of the freezer — this indicates a defrost system fault
Allow the fridge to run for 24 hours after cleaning coils before concluding it has not improved
advanced_fixes: A faulty door seal can be replaced by ordering the correct part number and pressing it into the door channel — cost $20–$60
Evaporator fan motor replacement is a DIY repair on most models — cost $30–$80 in parts
Refrigerant issues (no cooling despite compressor running) require a certified technician with handling equipment — call an appliance repair service
doNot: Do not use a sharp object to defrost ice buildup — pierce the evaporator coil and the fridge is written off
Do not attempt to recharge refrigerant yourself — it requires certification and specialised tools
Do not place hot food directly in the fridge — it forces the compressor to work excessively
lifespanNotes: Condenser cleaning and seal replacement are cheap, high-impact fixes. Compressor and refrigerant issues in older fridges may not be economical to repair.

causes: Condenser or evaporator fan blade partially obstructed by ice or debris
Fridge not level, causing compressor vibration to resonate through the frame
Items stored on top of the fridge vibrating with compressor operation
Drain pan beneath the fridge loose and rattling
beginner_fixes: Identify when the noise occurs: during compressor cycles, constantly, or intermittently — this narrows the cause significantly
Check that the fridge is level using a spirit level — adjust the front feet until level
Remove everything from the top of the fridge — loose items amplify compressor vibrations
Pull the fridge away from the wall and check that no pipe or tube at the back is vibrating against the cabinet
intermediate_fixes: Remove the lower back panel to inspect the condenser fan — clean with a brush and check that it spins freely
Check the drain pan (usually beneath the fridge, accessed from the front) is seated correctly in its clips
A gurgling noise is normal and indicates refrigerant flow — this is not a fault
advanced_fixes: If the noise is a grinding or scraping from inside the freezer, ice may have built up around the evaporator fan — defrost completely (unplug for 24 hours) and restart
A failing compressor produces a loud knocking or clicking sound before each start cycle — compressor replacement is expensive; compare cost vs. appliance age
Fan motor replacement for condenser or evaporator fans: $30–$80 and accessible with basic tools on most models
doNot: Do not ignore a loud knocking sound from the compressor — it may indicate imminent compressor failure
Do not place the fridge directly on carpet — use a hard floor mat to reduce vibration and improve airflow
Do not dismiss a continuous clicking sound — it often means the compressor is failing to start
lifespanNotes: Most noise issues are mechanical and inexpensive to resolve. A fridge making noise is still working — address it before it progresses to a cooling failure.

causes: Defrost drain blocked with food debris, causing meltwater to overflow onto the floor
Door seals failing and allowing warm air in, creating excess condensation
Water supply line to ice maker or water dispenser cracked or loose
Drain pan cracked or overflowing due to high ambient humidity
beginner_fixes: Identify where the water is coming from: under the fridge, inside the fridge, or from the back
Check the defrost drain at the back wall of the freezer — pour warm water into it to clear a blockage
Check the door seals for tears or gaps by inspecting the entire perimeter
If the fridge has a water dispenser or ice maker, inspect the supply line connection at the back
intermediate_fixes: To clear the defrost drain: unplug, remove all food, and use a turkey baster with warm water to flush the drain hole
Clean the drain pan beneath the fridge — if it is cracked, order a replacement; cost $15–$40
In humid climates, some external condensation is normal — check if it's worse when the door seals are failing
advanced_fixes: A fully blocked defrost drain may require the back panel of the freezer to be removed and the drain to be cleared manually
Water supply line replacement: turn off the water supply valve, disconnect the line, and replace with a new braided stainless line; cost $10–$25
Persistent internal condensation after seal replacement may indicate a refrigerant issue — call a technician
doNot: Do not ignore water pooling on the floor — it creates a slipping hazard and can warp flooring
Do not use a sharp object to poke the defrost drain — you risk puncturing the evaporator
Do not leave the fridge running if the water source is the compressor compartment — this may indicate a refrigerant line issue
lifespanNotes: Most leaks are caused by a blocked defrost drain or failing door seal — both are inexpensive fixes that extend the life of the appliance significantly.

causes: Ice maker turned off via the arm or switch on the unit
Water supply line to the ice maker kinked, frozen, or shut off
Ice bin full and the ice maker paused production automatically
Water inlet valve faulty, preventing water from entering the ice maker
beginner_fixes: Locate the ice maker's on/off arm or switch and confirm it is in the 'ON' position
Check that the ice bin is not full and that ice hasn't clumped into a solid block — break any clumps up
Verify the water supply valve behind the fridge is fully open
Check your home water pressure — ice makers require a minimum of 20 psi
intermediate_fixes: Inspect the water supply line at the back of the fridge for kinks or a section that may have frozen
Pour warm water along the supply line if you suspect it is frozen
Run a test cycle on the ice maker if your model supports it — check your user manual
advanced_fixes: Test the water inlet valve with a multimeter for continuity — a faulty valve will show no continuity and requires replacement; cost $30–$80
Ice maker assembly replacement: if the unit is over 5 years old and the motor or thermostat has failed, a complete module replacement ($80–$200) may be more practical than individual component repair
Check the freezer temperature — it must be at or below -12°C (10°F) for ice production to function
doNot: Do not use a knife or sharp object to break up ice clumps inside the ice bin — use warm water
Do not reconnect the water line without checking it is fully secured — a loose fitting causes leaks inside the cabinet
Do not assume the ice maker is broken after a power cut — it can take 24 hours to resume normal production
lifespanNotes: Most ice maker issues are supply line or setting related and cost nothing to fix. Module replacement is cost-effective if the refrigerator is otherwise in good condition.

causes: Drain pump filter blocked with lint, coins, or small clothing items
Drain hose kinked, crushed, or installed at an incorrect height
Drain pump motor failed, unable to expel water
Selected programme does not include a drain cycle (e.g. a soak or hand-wash setting)
beginner_fixes: Check you are not on a pause or soak programme — select a Spin or Drain cycle and press Start
Check the drain hose at the back for kinks and ensure the end is not submerged in standing water in the drain standpipe
Place towels down and locate the drain pump filter — usually behind a small panel at the bottom front of the machine
Slowly open the filter cap to drain water (have a shallow tray ready) then remove and clean the filter
intermediate_fixes: Check inside the filter housing for coins, buttons, or bra underwires — these are the most common blockage items
Inspect the entire length of the drain hose for blockages — disconnect and blow through it to confirm it is clear
Run a hot maintenance wash at 60°C with a washing machine cleaner to clear any partial blockages
advanced_fixes: If the pump filter is clear and the hose is clear, the pump motor may have failed — access varies by model but is typically reached from the back or bottom panel
A replacement drain pump costs $30–$80 and is a DIY replacement on most front-loader models
Use a multimeter to test the pump motor for continuity before purchasing a replacement
doNot: Do not open the front door while water is still in the drum — it will flood the floor
Do not force the drum door open — many machines have a door interlock that prevents opening mid-cycle for safety
Do not run the machine again without clearing the filter first — it will simply fail to drain again
lifespanNotes: Filter cleaning is a maintenance task that should be done every 3 months. A blocked pump filter is the cause of drainage failures in the majority of cases.

diagnosis: Washing machine not completing spin cycle
causes: Unbalanced load causing the machine to detect imbalance and abort the spin
Drain not fully completed before spin — partially blocked pump or hose
Lid switch or door interlock faulty, preventing spin for safety
Drive belt worn or snapped, disconnecting the drum from the motor
beginner_fixes: Redistribute the load manually — a single heavy item (jeans, a towel) on one side will always cause an imbalance abort
Reduce the load size — overloading prevents the drum reaching spin speed
Select a Spin Only cycle to test the spin independently of the wash cycle
Check that the machine door/lid is firmly closed and the latch clicks
intermediate_fixes: Check if water remains in the drum — the machine will not spin if it cannot first drain; resolve any drainage issue first
Inspect the door interlock/lid switch — if the machine thinks the door is open, it won't spin; test by pressing the door firmly and listening for the click
Check for an error code on the display — consult your model's user manual for the spin-related error codes
advanced_fixes: Access the rear or bottom panel and inspect the drive belt — if it is stretched, cracked, or broken, it needs replacing; cost $10–$30
A faulty door interlock (latch mechanism) replacement costs $20–$50 and is reachable with basic tools
Carbon brush replacement on the motor is needed on some older models — a worn brush prevents the motor reaching spin speed
doNot: Do not overload the drum — this is the single most common cause of spin failures and also damages the bearings over time
Do not force the door open mid-cycle — the interlock is a safety feature
Do not ignore unusual grinding or squealing sounds during spin — this indicates bearing wear which worsens rapidly
lifespanNotes: Load balancing and filter cleaning resolve most spin issues at zero cost. Drive belt replacement is affordable and restores full function.

causes: Door gasket (rubber seal on front-loaders) torn, cracked, or accumulating mould
Too much detergent or incorrect detergent type causing excessive suds overflow
Inlet hose connection loose or washer seal perished
Drain pump housing cracked or pump filter cap not tightened after maintenance
beginner_fixes: Identify exactly where the water is coming from — front door, back connections, or underneath
Check whether you are using HE (High Efficiency) detergent if you have an HE machine — standard detergent causes excessive suds and overflow
Use the correct detergent dose — more detergent does not clean better and always causes leaks
Check inlet hose connections at both the tap and the back of the machine — hand-tighten if loose
intermediate_fixes: Inspect the door gasket on front-loaders for tears, holes, or accumulated debris — clean with a damp cloth and check for damage
Run an empty cycle and observe carefully — identify the precise moment and location the leak occurs
Check the soap dispenser drawer for blockages — a blocked dispenser causes water to overflow from the drawer
advanced_fixes: Door gasket replacement on a front-loader: access via the front panel, peel the gasket from its retaining rings, and fit the new seal — cost $30–$80 in parts
Replace the inlet hose if the rubber washers inside the connectors are perished — new washers are $2 or a replacement hose is $10–$20
A cracked drum or tub is a major repair — compare repair cost with appliance replacement
doNot: Do not use standard detergent in a high-efficiency machine — it always causes leaking and can damage the pump
Do not ignore mould on the door gasket — it causes odours, damages the seal, and can cause leaks
Do not overtighten the inlet hose connections with tools — hand-tight is correct; overtightening cracks the plastic fittings
lifespanNotes: Detergent issues and inlet hose leaks are free to resolve. Door gasket replacement is a straightforward repair that restores a watertight seal.

diagnosis: Microwave operating but not heating food
causes: Magnetron tube failed — the component that generates microwave energy
High-voltage diode failed, preventing the magnetron from receiving sufficient voltage
Door interlock switch faulty, cutting power to the magnetron as a safety measure
High-voltage capacitor failed
beginner_fixes: Test with a mug of water: microwave for 1 minute on full power — water should be hot; if not, the heating system has failed
Check the power level is set to 100% (P-100) and not a low power level
Confirm the microwave is completing its cycle and not being interrupted mid-cook
Check whether the rotating ring and turntable are correctly seated — a displaced turntable can sometimes trigger a fault sensor
intermediate_fixes: Check and test all three door interlock switches — a faulty switch is the most safely accessible repair and costs $5–$15 per switch
Reset the microwave by unplugging for 2 minutes then plugging back in
If the microwave hums and sounds normal but food stays cold, the magnetron has almost certainly failed
advanced_fixes: WARNING: The high-voltage capacitor inside a microwave stores lethal charge (up to 2000V) even when unplugged — do not open the casing without discharging it
Magnetron replacement: the part costs $50–$150 but requires high-voltage safety knowledge — strongly recommend professional repair
For microwaves under $150: compare repair cost with replacement — a new unit may be more economical
doNot: Do not open the microwave casing without discharging the capacitor — it stores lethal voltage even when unplugged
Do not operate the microwave with the door open or with a damaged door seal
Do not attempt magnetron replacement without proper electrical safety training
lifespanNotes: A non-heating microwave usually indicates magnetron failure. Given the high-voltage hazard and repair cost, replacement is often the better economic decision for units over 5 years old.

causes: Metal object, metallic trim, or foil inside the microwave
Waveguide cover (the flat panel on the interior wall) coated in food splatter and burning
Chipped or worn interior paint exposing bare metal
Metal rack or turntable ring incorrectly positioned
beginner_fixes: Stop the microwave immediately — do not continue operating it while sparking
Check for any metal items, foil, or metallic-edged crockery inside
Inspect the waveguide cover on the interior ceiling or side wall — if it is discoloured, burnt, or has holes, this is the cause
Clean the interior thoroughly — any large food deposits, especially fat splatter, can arc
intermediate_fixes: Remove and replace the waveguide cover — it is a cardboard or mica sheet held by one or two clips; replacement covers cost $5–$15 and are model-specific
If the interior paint is chipped, apply microwave-safe interior paint to reseal the exposed metal — available online for $10–$15
Run an empty 30-second test after cleaning to confirm the sparking has stopped before cooking food
advanced_fixes: If sparking continues after cleaning and waveguide cover replacement, the magnetron antenna tip may be damaged — this requires professional inspection
A heavily burnt waveguide cover that has created carbonisation on the cavity wall requires thorough cleaning before the new cover is fitted
Persistent arcing with no visible cause may indicate a faulty stirrer motor
doNot: Do not continue running a sparking microwave — it can cause a fire
Do not use aluminium foil in the microwave under any circumstances
Do not use crockery with metallic trim or gold/silver decoration in the microwave
lifespanNotes: Waveguide cover replacement is one of the cheapest and most effective microwave repairs. Addressing sparking promptly prevents permanent damage to the cavity.

causes: Turntable ring or roller guide misaligned or broken
Food debris jamming the turntable coupling or roller ring
Turntable motor failed
Coupler (the plastic D-shaped connector) cracked or worn
beginner_fixes: Remove the turntable plate and roller ring and clean the floor of the microwave cavity — debris is the most common cause
Check the roller ring is seated correctly in its circular track and that all three wheels are intact
Check the coupler on the motor shaft — it must be fully engaged with the bottom of the turntable plate
Confirm the turntable is not deactivated — some models have a Turntable On/Off button
intermediate_fixes: Inspect the coupler (plastic D-shaped piece on the floor) for cracks — replacements cost $3–$10 and are model-specific
Check that the roller ring legs are not cracked — if one leg is broken, the ring wobbles and jams; replacement ring costs $5–$15
Run the microwave empty and listen for the motor sound from beneath the cavity floor — silence indicates motor failure
advanced_fixes: Turntable motor replacement requires accessing the base of the microwave — unplug, remove the base plate, disconnect the two motor wires, fit new motor; cost $15–$40
Confirm the motor voltage is correct before ordering a replacement — check the motor label for voltage and RPM specifications
If the microwave heats food without the turntable rotating, cooking is still safe but uneven — rotate food manually or repair promptly
doNot: Do not force the turntable if it feels jammed — identify the obstruction first
Do not use the microwave without the turntable plate or roller ring unless the manual specifies it is safe to do so
Do not order a replacement motor without confirming the model number — turntable motors are not universal
lifespanNotes: Turntable faults are almost always inexpensive to resolve. A replacement coupler or roller ring for $5–$15 fixes the majority of cases.

diagnosis: Air conditioner running but not cooling effectively
causes: Air filter heavily clogged, restricting airflow across the evaporator coil
Refrigerant level low due to a slow leak
Evaporator coil iced over, blocking all heat exchange
Outdoor condenser unit clogged with leaves and debris, unable to reject heat
beginner_fixes: Check and replace or clean the air filter — a clogged filter is responsible for the majority of reduced cooling performance
Ensure all room windows and doors are closed while the AC is running
Check the thermostat setting — confirm it is set to COOL mode and the set temperature is below the current room temperature
Inspect the outdoor unit for debris, vegetation, or objects blocking the grille
intermediate_fixes: Check for ice on the indoor unit coil — if iced over, turn the AC to FAN ONLY for 2 hours to defrost before cooling again
Clean the outdoor condenser coil with a garden hose (from the inside out, with the power off)
Check that supply registers in each room are open and not blocked by furniture
If the unit runs continuously without reaching the set temperature, inspect the refrigerant level (requires a technician)
advanced_fixes: Refrigerant recharge requires a certified HVAC technician — low refrigerant always indicates a leak that must be repaired first
Evaporator coil cleaning with a no-rinse foam cleaner improves efficiency significantly on units over 3 years old
If the compressor is short-cycling (turning on and off rapidly), a capacitor may have failed — a common repair costing $15–$50 in parts
doNot: Do not attempt to add refrigerant yourself — it requires certification and the leak must be found and repaired first
Do not block the area around the outdoor unit with plant growth or storage
Do not run the AC with a frozen evaporator coil — it causes compressor damage
lifespanNotes: Filter replacement and coil cleaning are annual maintenance tasks that maintain full cooling efficiency. Neglecting these typically cuts cooling capacity by 20–40%.

causes: Circuit breaker tripped due to a momentary overload or power surge
Thermostat batteries dead or thermostat settings misconfigured
Safety float switch triggered by condensate drain backup
Capacitor failure preventing the compressor or fan motor from starting
beginner_fixes: Check the circuit breaker panel — reset any tripped breaker for the AC circuit (turn fully OFF then ON)
Replace thermostat batteries and confirm the thermostat is set to COOL with a temperature below the room temperature
Check the indoor unit for a reset button and press it
Inspect the power cord and wall switch (if present) for window units
intermediate_fixes: Check the condensate drain pan — a full pan triggers a float safety switch that shuts the unit off; drain and clean the pan
After resetting a tripped breaker, wait 30 minutes before attempting to restart — some protection circuits have a time delay
Check whether the outdoor unit has its own disconnect box — confirm its fuse or breaker is intact
advanced_fixes: A failed capacitor is indicated by a humming sound when the unit tries to start but cannot — capacitor replacement is a common DIY repair; cost $10–$50
Discharge the capacitor before handling — use an insulated screwdriver across the terminals
If the breaker trips repeatedly after resetting, there is an electrical fault in the unit — call an HVAC technician before using the circuit again
doNot: Do not repeatedly reset a tripping breaker — a breaker that trips repeatedly indicates a fault that must be investigated
Do not attempt to bypass the float safety switch — it prevents water damage to your ceiling and floors
Do not handle capacitors without discharging them — they store charge and can cause serious injury
lifespanNotes: Most no-power issues are inexpensive to resolve. A tripped breaker or dead thermostat batteries are the most common causes and cost nothing to fix.

causes: Condensate drain line blocked with algae, mould, or debris
Dirty air filter restricting airflow and causing the evaporator coil to ice up and drip on defrost
Unit not level, causing condensate to overflow toward the indoor side
Drain pan cracked or corroded
beginner_fixes: Inspect the air filter immediately — a dirty filter is the most common indirect cause of AC water leaks
Locate the condensate drain line outlet (usually a white PVC pipe near the outdoor unit or into a drain) and check if it is dripping or blocked
For window units, check that the rear of the unit tilts slightly downward — this directs condensate outside
Turn off the unit if water is dripping onto electrical components or flooring
intermediate_fixes: Flush the condensate drain line: attach a wet/dry vacuum to the drain line access port and clear the blockage, or use a drain line flush tablet
Pour a cup of distilled white vinegar into the drain line access port monthly to prevent algae buildup
Inspect the drain pan for cracks — small cracks can be sealed with waterproof epoxy; larger damage requires pan replacement
advanced_fixes: If the drain line is severely blocked, use a drain snake or call an HVAC technician to clear it with nitrogen
Install a float switch on the drain pan if one is not already present — it will automatically shut off the unit if the drain backs up again
A technician should check the refrigerant level if the coil is repeatedly icing and causing drips after all drain and filter fixes
doNot: Do not ignore water leaking near the electrical components of the unit — it is an electrocution and short-circuit risk
Do not seal the drain line outlet — it must be open to drain condensate
Do not allow water to pool repeatedly on the ceiling or wall — structural damage accrues quickly
lifespanNotes: Drain line maintenance every 3–6 months prevents this issue entirely. A monthly vinegar flush is the most effective preventive measure.
